newsitem.title: ITALY: Italians who don't pay tax may have cars impounded.
newsitem.headline: Italians who don't pay tax may have cars impounded.

text.p: Plans by the Italian government to stop tax evaders from using their vehicles ran into howls of protest on Friday.
The sanctions were introduced by the government when it drew up a package of fiscal measures last week to complete the 1997 budget and were published in the Official Gazette.
They mean that people who do not pay taxes after an assessment risk having use of their moveable goods, including cars, motorcycles or boats, blocked by the authorities.
Fines could follow. A vehicle would be impounded if a person ignored the ban.
Italian newspapers dubbed the measures "fiscal clamping" and trade associations said they were outraged.
"Now we are waiting for a reintrodution of the pillory," Ivano Spalanzani, president of the artisans' association Confartigianato, said in a statement.
"You can't blockade the cars of people who do not pay taxes because their business is in crisis," he added.
Italy's centre-left government has pledged to wage war on tax evasion, which is widespread.
In another controversial move, tax police last month set up a free-phone hotline to encourage Italians to report people who fiddle their taxes.
